premises.text: Enterprise rapid prototyping/advanced manufacturing is cumbersome: designers and machine operators shuttle Excel/spreadsheets across heterogeneous machine software, often across decentralized sites
premises.evidence_span: all day, they go back and forth with Excel files, spreadsheets, file shares. It's a very cumbersome process

premises.text: Zap is a cloud manufacturing platform that connects 3D printers, CNC, waterjets, welding, and assembly workflows for one-click remote job control, live render, and factory duplication via a fog client
Monetized via about $200K per site license to large enterprises

value.text: Go from design to a real manufactured object instantly, anytime, anywhere
value.evidence_span: taking an idea to a real object instantly, anytime, anywhere

causal_links.evidence_span: time to market is one of the most important things when you're trying to beat your competition
connecting all these machines and workflows in the cloud, anytime, anywhere
looking to be more efficient as they scale worldwide

notes: Heterogeneous machine software, manual operation, and multi-site decentralization folded as one workflow problem (§4.1.6). Prior 3D OS traction and 75k parts excluded. Demo print/CNC/weld/assembly/duplicate-factory steps folded as one Zap platform cascade (§4.1.7). Ford/Cisco named as enterprise evidence of site-license GTM, not separate premises. Anti-template: problem, platform, and licensing separately revisable.
